correctness.rationale: The 2011 sharp bounds imply gamma_P(Q5)=4. The exact finite verification covers every four-vertex subset of a 32-vertex graph, using correct monotone power-domination closure (both synchronous and sequential versions). The Python script partitions all 3600 successes into six exact group orbits, checks every possible single-token exchange, counts 70400 oriented TJ moves and none with adjacent endpoints, and performs six representative BFS searches; isometry-invariance extends their eccentricity values to all states. The C++17 script independently reconstructs the 3600 states, 35200 edges and zero TS edges and exhaustively computes all 3600 eccentricities. Both programs were compiled/executed from included paths and the output was checked. These finite computations prove only the finite classification, no unbounded claims.

originality.rationale: The new result is the complete 3600-state, six-orbit classification and exact TS/TJ transition geometry of the five-cube, not the previously established cardinality four. The four-page 2011 hypercube paper provides cardinality bounds but not a classification of optimal sets. The 2015 product-graph source provides a generalized power-domination lower bound; the 2026 general reconfiguration source provides a universal framework and separate examples, with TS for power domination proposed for further study. Searches of relevant named aliases and a searchable record collection revealed no exact five-cube orbit or metric census. The incompletely accessible Pai–Chiu conference note and non-indexed computations are residual priority risks, not represented as checked full texts.
residual_risks: The full Pai–Chiu 2012 conference note was not retrieved; it may contain additional state-count detail not visible in its abstract.
Unindexed or independently conducted finite enumerations could establish some of the exact same figures; searches and accessible history cannot establish global uniqueness.
The result is a single finite host classification, not a theorem for all hypercubes.

value.rationale: The five-cube is the first dimension for which four monitoring units are required, following the smaller two-unit cube, and is the first natural nontrivial enumeration layer after the known hypercube cardinality bounds. Complete classification of its optimal placements by all Hamming symmetries and their move graph is a motivated robustness/reconfiguration invariant. The unexpected gap between total local slide immobility and global unrestricted exchange connectivity of exact radius five/diameter six is structurally informative; the exact degree spectrum supplies reusable finite benchmarks. The result is not just a known cardinality or an arbitrary numerical slice; no larger-dimensional extrapolation is suggested.
